title: Saudi point-of-sale spending, Q2 2024 vs Q2 2023

attempts.text: Saudi Arabia's point-of-sale card spending (SAMA) experienced a significant increase in Q2 2024 compared to Q2 2023, with a 4.2% increase in the average weekly POS value. This increase is attributed to a 4.2% increase in the average weekly transactions, which were up 15.8% from Q2 2023. The increase in transactions is primarily driven by an increase in the average weekly value of Miscellaneous Goods and Services, which increased by SAR 301 million. This increase in value is primarily due to an increase in the average weekly value of Clothing and Footwear, which increased by SAR 191 million. The increase in value of Restaurants & Café is also significant, with an increase of SAR 122 million. The increase in value of Gas Stations is also notable, with an increase of SAR 108 million. The increase in value of Public Utilities is also significant, with an increase of SAR 27 million. The largest movers (by size of change) in Q2 2024 are Miscellaneous Goods and Services, Clothing and Footwear, Restaurants & Café, Gas Stations, and Public Utilities.

final_text: Average weekly point-of-sale spending in Saudi Arabia was SAR 12.25 bn in Q2 2024, up 4.2% from SAR 11.76 bn in Q2 2023. Average weekly transactions were 193.8 million (up 15.8%), and the average ticket was SAR 63.2 (down 10.0%). The largest movements were: Miscellaneous Goods and Services increased by SAR 301 mn; Clothing and Footwear decreased by SAR 191 mn; Restaurants & Café increased by SAR 122 mn.
